Finnish

[edit]
Finnish Wikipedia has an article on:
pornografia
Wikipedia fi

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism (see French pornographie). Contains the suffix -grafia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpornoˌɡrɑfiɑ/, [ˈpo̞rno̞ˌɡrɑ̝fiɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -ɑfiɑ
  • Syllabification(key): por‧no‧gra‧fi‧a, por‧nog‧ra‧fi‧a
  • Hyphenation(key): porno‧grafia, por‧nog‧ra‧fia

Noun

[edit]

pornografia

  1. pornography

Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
pornografia
Wikipedia it

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin pornographia, from Ancient Greek πορνογράφος (pornográphos).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Rhymes: -ia
  • IPA(key): /por.no.ɡraˈfi.a/, /ˌpɔr.no.ɡraˈfi.a/[1]
  • Rhymes: -ia
  • Hyphenation: por‧no‧gra‧fì‧a

Noun

[edit]

pornografia f (plural pornografie)

  1. pornography

Related terms

[edit]

  1. ^ pornografia in Luciano Canepari, Dizionario di Pronuncia Italiana (DiPI)

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
pornografia
Wikipedia pl

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French pornographie, from Ancient Greek πορνογράφος (pornográphos), from πορνεία (porneía, “fornication, prostitution”) + γράφω (gráphō, “to depict”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pɔr.nɔˈɡra.fja/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -afja
  • Syllabification: por‧no‧gra‧fia

Noun

[edit]

pornografia f

  1. pornography (depiction of sexual subject matter with prurient intent)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of pornografia
singular
nominative pornografia
genitive pornografii
dative pornografii
accusative pornografię
instrumental pornografią
locative pornografii
vocative pornografio

Derived terms

[edit]
adjective
  • pornograficzny

Related terms

[edit]
nouns
  • pornograf
  • pornos

  • porno-

  • pornografia in Polish dictionaries at PWN
